bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists where the isolate level can be decreased even if it is already zero.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced a MemorySanitizer READ SEGV in `get_adjacent_run` at `lib/fribidi-bidi.c:156`. The 284-byte witness is interpreted as 71 little-endian `FriBidiChar` code points: 47xU+202D (LRO), 2xU+2068 (FSI), 14xU+202D (LRO), U+2068 (FSI), 3xU+2069 (PDI), 3xU+2067 (RLI), and U+0800 (SAMARITAN LETTER ALAF). `fribidi_get_bidi_types` and `run_list_encode_bidi_types` preserve that exact run order. In `fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels_ex`, the first two FSI runs push the only two real isolate frames, the later `LRO(14)` sequence raises `level` to 124 and leaves `over_pushed` nonzero, and the third FSI scans `PDI,PDI,PDI,RLI,RLI,RLI,U+0800`. Because line 745 tests outer `valid_isolate_count` instead of local `isolate_count`, the scan survives the three PDI decrements, returns local `isolate_count` to 0 on the third RLI, sees U+0800 as the first strong RTL run, and computes `new_level = 125`. That increments `valid_isolate_count` to 3 but, with `over_pushed` already set, `PUSH_STATUS` does not push a third isolate frame. The first two PDI runs then pop the only two real isolate frames, so by the third PDI `isolate_level` is already 0 while `valid_isolate_count` is still 1. The unconditional `isolate_level--` underflows it to -1, the following RLI snapshots `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL == -1` before incrementing the local counter back to 0, and the isolate-connection pass indexes `run_per_isolate_level[-1]` on both runs. That negative-index isolate-link-table access is the first fully source-grounded memory-safety sink; the saved MSan crash later occurs in `get_adjacent_run` when weak-type resolution consumes isolate links after that corruption, but `runtime_disambiguation` is disabled so the exact crashing link is not statically pinned down here.

source.description: Maps each attacker-controlled `FriBidiChar` from the witness into the bidi-type stream consumed by the vulnerable paragraph-embedding algorithm.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_34695/poc`, which `bin/fribidi-fuzzer.c` passes to FriBidi as a 71-element `FriBidiChar` array.
source.note: On the witness, this writes the type sequence `LRO(47), FSI, FSI, LRO(14), FSI, PDI, PDI, PDI, RLI, RLI, RLI, R`, where the trailing `R` comes from U+0800 (SAMARITAN LETTER ALAF).

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The PDI close-isolate path decrements `isolate_level` even when the real isolate stack is already empty, so the third PDI underflows it from 0 to -1 and stores a negative isolate level into later logic.
root_cause.note: The fix in `patch.diff` replaces the unconditional decrement with `if (isolate_level>0) isolate_level--;`, preventing the negative isolate level that feeds the out-of-bounds table access.

sink.description: Direct source-grounded unsafe access. The isolate-connection pass indexes `run_per_isolate_level` with `isolate_level == -1`, reading one slot before the stack array and then reusing that same invalid slot while wiring isolate links.
sink.note: This is the first proven memory-safety violation in the staged vulnerable source. The saved MemorySanitizer SEGV happens later in `get_adjacent_run` when weak-type resolution consumes isolate links built after this corruption, but `runtime_disambiguation` is disabled so the exact crashing link is not source-disambiguated here.

tainted_value_origin.description: Stores each attacker-derived bidi class into a `FriBidiRun`, creating the exact run sequence that later drives `level`, `over_pushed`, `valid_isolate_count`, and `isolate_level`.
tainted_value_origin.note: Because the surrounding split condition includes `FRIBIDI_IS_ISOLATE(char_type)`, every witness FSI/PDI/RLI stays a one-character run instead of being merged.

parser_admitted.description: The witness has passed the non-empty fast path and has been admitted into FriBidi's paragraph-embedding algorithm as a run list; execution does not return at `if (!len)`.

fine_trace.note: Maps each witness code point into a FriBidi bidi class. The staged 71-code-point buffer becomes `LRO(47), FSI, FSI, LRO(14), FSI, PDI, PDI, PDI, RLI, RLI, RLI, R`, where the final `R` is U+0800.

Encodes the converted types into `main_run_list`. Because the split condition includes `FRIBIDI_IS_ISOLATE(char_type)`, each witness FSI/PDI/RLI stays a one-character run and the later explicit-level loop sees the same run order.
Processing the leading `LRO(47)` run applies the explicit-level formula 47 times, raising the current embedding level to 94 and pushing only non-isolate override frames.

The first two FSI runs both compute valid new levels (96 then 98). Each records its current isolate level, increments local `isolate_level`, increments `valid_isolate_count`, pushes a real isolate frame, and leaves the algorithm at `level == 98`, `isolate_level == 2`, `valid_isolate_count == 2`.

The later `LRO(14)` run consumes the remaining even levels after 98. Thirteen LROs push to `level == 124`; the fourteenth computes `new_level == 126`, so it is rejected and increments `over_pushed` while leaving the stack with only the two FSI isolate frames beneath the 13 later LRO frames.

The third FSI scans the suffix `PDI, PDI, PDI, RLI, RLI, RLI, U+0800`. Its local `isolate_count` drops from 0 to -3 across the three PDI runs, but line 745 tests outer `valid_isolate_count` instead of local `isolate_count`, so the scan does not break; the three following RLIs then increment local `isolate_count` back to 0.

After the third RLI restores local `isolate_count` to 0, the following U+0800 run is the first strong letter visible to the scan. `fsi_base_level` therefore becomes RTL and the third FSI computes `new_level == 125`.

Because `new_level <= FRIBIDI_BIDI_MAX_EXPLICIT_LEVEL`, the third FSI is counted as valid: `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(pp)` is recorded as 2, local `isolate_level` increments to 3, `valid_isolate_count` becomes 3, and line 776 sets `level = 125`. But `PUSH_STATUS` is suppressed because `over_pushed` is already nonzero, so no third isolate frame is pushed.

On the first PDI, the close-isolate branch consumes the two carried rejected-code counts, pops the 13 later LRO frames until the next stack entry is an isolate, then pops the second real isolate frame. After line 710, local `isolate_level` is 1 and `valid_isolate_count` is 2.

The second PDI encounters an isolate frame immediately, so the while-loop does not run. `POP_STATUS` restores the first FSI state and the following decrement takes its stored `isolate_level` from 1 to 0, leaving `valid_isolate_count == 1` and no isolate frames on the stack.

Root cause. The third PDI still takes the `valid_isolate_count > 0` branch because step 8 incremented that counter without pushing a matching frame. Its preceding while-loop empties the remaining leading LRO frames, `POP_STATUS` does nothing with `stack_size == 0`, and the unconditional decrement underflows `isolate_level` from 0 to -1; this PDI stores `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(pp) == -1`.

The following RLI is processed while local `isolate_level` is still -1, so line 765 records `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(pp) == -1` for that run before line 767 increments the local counter back to 0. The connection pass will therefore see two consecutive runs with negative isolate level: this RLI and the preceding PDI.

Sink. In the isolate-connection pass, `int isolate_level = RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(pp);` becomes -1 for the PDI from step 11 and again for the RLI from step 12. The block at lines 816-821 therefore reads `run_per_isolate_level[-1]` and writes the same one-before-array slot back via `run_per_isolate_level[isolate_level] = pp`, making this the first proven out-of-bounds access in the staged vulnerable source.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: No at exact sink-step level. The source-grounded sink is the earlier negative-index access to `run_per_isolate_level` at `lib/fribidi-bidi.c:816-821`; the saved MSan SEGV occurs later at `get_adjacent_run:156` when weak-type resolution consumes isolate links after that corruption.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes through the reviewed project frames. The saved stack `get_adjacent_run -> fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels_ex -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` is a later manifestation in the same call after fine-trace step 13's negative-index isolate-link-table access. With `runtime_disambiguation=false`, the staged artifacts do not pin down the exact link field loaded at `get_adjacent_run:150` before the line-156 crash.

poc.trigger: When `bin/fribidi-fuzzer.c` interprets the staged 284-byte witness as 71 `FriBidiChar` values, the exact `LRO(47), FSI, FSI, LRO(14), FSI, PDI, PDI, PDI, RLI, RLI, RLI, U+0800` layout makes the third PDI store `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL == -1`, makes the following RLI inherit `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL == -1`, and causes the later isolate-connection pass to access `run_per_isolate_level[-1]`; the saved Stage 01 run then crashes downstream in `get_adjacent_run` while consuming isolate links after that corruption.

format.name: FriBidi UTF-32LE code-point buffer
format.contract: A 284-byte little-endian `FriBidiChar` buffer whose 71 code points are exactly 47xU+202D, 2xU+2068, 14xU+202D, U+2068, 3xU+2069, 3xU+2067, and U+0800. That exact layout yields the run sequence `LRO(47), FSI, FSI, LRO(14), FSI, PDI, PDI, PDI, RLI, RLI, RLI, R`, leaves `valid_isolate_count` one isolate ahead of the real isolate stack, and makes the connection pass reach `run_per_isolate_level[-1]`.
